appearance_facts.fact: The Product A bar is a short dark red vertical rectangle whose top edge sits just below the 2,000 gridline.
The Product E bar is a tall dark red vertical rectangle reaching just under the 8,000 gridline.
The Product C bar is a short dark red vertical rectangle slightly above the 2,000 gridline.
The Product D bar is the tallest dark red vertical rectangle, reaching the 10,000 gridline.
The Product B bar is a medium-tall dark red vertical rectangle at the 6,000 gridline.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title: 'Units Sold by Product (Weekend Pop-up)'
Y-axis label 'Units Sold' with ticks at 2,000, 4,000, 6,000, 8,000, 10,000.
X-axis label 'Product' with categories Product E, Product A, Product C, Product D, Product B.
Product A's bar height corresponds to approximately 1,800 units (just below the 2,000 tick).
Product C's bar height corresponds to approximately 2,200 units (just above the 2,000 tick).
Product E's bar height corresponds to approximately 7,800 units (just below the 8,000 tick).
Product D's bar height corresponds to 10,000 units.
Product B's bar height corresponds to 6,000 units.

public_definitions: >= 1,000 and < 2,000 units: Low-sales review queue activation level
< 500 units from a decision threshold: Manual merchandising verification variance band
>= 6,000 and < 9,000 units: Expanded replenishment planning level
uncertain: Product A's exact unit value is not labeled; it is read visually as just under 2,000, placing it in the 1,000–2,000 band, but the precise distance from the 2,000 threshold is not numerically stated.
